findings.evidence: Integral.lean:147-148 is `((isBernsteinFunction_const hc).add (hf.isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive hcont)).congr fun _ _ ↦ rfl` — `halfLinePrimitive` appears only as the argument. `isBernsteinFunction_const` (Basic.lean:165) and `IsBernsteinFunction.add` (Basic.lean:140) already exist; `grep -rn "const_add" TauCeti/Analysis/CompletelyMonotone/` shows no Bernstein `const_add`.
findings.fix: Add `IsBernsteinFunction.const_add (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) : IsBernsteinFunction (fun t => c + f t)` to Bernstein/Basic.lean next to `add`/`smul`, with the same body, and delete both primitive-specific variants; callers write `(hf.isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive hcont).const_add hc`.
findings.issue: `isBernsteinFunction_const_add_halfLinePrimitive` (and its `IsCompletelyMonotone` twin at line 168) proves a special case of a general fact: `c + g` is Bernstein for any Bernstein `g` and `c ≥ 0`. The proof uses no property of `halfLinePrimitive`.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:65-66: "The open-half-line derivative condition is the standard one and permits boundary singularities such as the right derivative of `sqrt` at `0`"; Basic.lean:26-27 repeats that the definition "includes standard examples whose right derivative blows up at `0`". `IsBernsteinFunction` (Basic.lean:67-69) requires only `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)` and `ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ioi 0)`, never differentiability at `0`.
findings.fix: State the Bernstein results with `ContinuousOn f (Ioi 0)` (free from `hf.contDiffOn`) plus `∀ T, 0 < T → IntegrableOn f (Ioc 0 T)`, defining the primitive as `∫ x in Ioc 0 t, f x`; establish `HasDerivAt` only on `Ioi 0` (all `IsBernsteinFunction` needs) and continuity at `0` from dominated convergence. Keep the current `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)` statements as corollaries if desired.
findings.issue: `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)` is stronger than the result needs and excludes the motivating case. `f = fun x => x ^ (-1/2 : ℝ)` is completely monotone on `(0,∞)` and integrable at `0`, with primitive `2√t` a Bernstein function, but is not continuous on `Ici 0`, so this theorem cannot reach it. The `f (max x 0)` definition forces the excess hypothesis by demanding a two-sided derivative at `0`, which `IsBernsteinFunction` never requires.

findings.evidence: Integral.lean:121 — `(hcont 0 self_mem_Ici).tendsto.mono_left ...` is the sole use of `hcont`; the `0 < t` branch (line 118) uses only `hf.nonneg`.
findings.fix: Weaken to `(hcont : ContinuousWithinAt f (Ici 0) 0)` and replace `hcont 0 self_mem_Ici` with `hcont`; call sites pass `hcont 0 self_mem_Ici`.
findings.issue: `nonneg_of_continuousOn` assumes `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)` but the proof only ever uses continuity within `Ici 0` at the single point `0`.

summary: Two `const_add` lemmas are special cases of a general Bernstein closure fact that is one line and belongs in Basic.lean, and the `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)` hypothesis is stronger than the mathematics needs — it excludes `t ↦ 2√t`, the boundary-singularity example the predicate was explicitly designed to admit.
